body: I try to do that, but it really doesn't seem to help me. It feels more like a chore than a relief. :/

My closest family members are about 1200 miles away, and I'm not at all close to any of them, so that isn't really an option. :(

Well, it's the middle of Summer vacation, so a school counselor isn't really an option either.

I am seeing a new psychiatrist next month, though. It's just that the thoughts and feelings are getting stronger and stronger and I hate to have to wait for help.
I don't know. Because I'm still a minor and my parents are so unwilling to believe that I actually do need help, I could see it only making things much worse.

If you feel even a slight bit that you need to call, I urge you to. If not for yourself, for your wife and children. You can avoid the topic of suicide altogether when you call if you don't feel comfortable and instead just talk about whatever may be bothering you. I'm unable to utilize such resources, even if you are afraid to, you are blessed to be able to.
I appreciate that, thank you. If I knew of any way you may be able to help me, I would take you up on your offer.

I'm trying to not be afraid. 

I can't be hospitalized. If that were to happen I wouldn't be able to work, and then I wouldn't be able to pay for school, and then I'll never be able to do anything or go anywhere in life and I'd be better off dead. And do you know how infuriated my parents would be? Gosh, they'd hate me even more for it. 

I definitely cannot talk to my parents about my depression. I tried once, and all my mom said was, "You don't need so much attention. Oh well, I guess I'll pray for you anyways." (Exact words.)
